verdict.root_cause: Not established. Every dispatch targeted cart, and cart is clean on all three signal types: span error ratio identically zero with no gaps [tr_6696564ceed5][tr_7f64a0cb0538], normal info-level store operations at both window boundaries [tr_185f3cb170bc], and sub-5ms handler and Valkey spans in the sampled traces [tr_326259fa9793]. Cart is where the investigation began, not where the fault is. The only directional hint is that in every sampled trace the degrading hop lies outside cart — in load-generator self-time, frontend route execution, or frontend-proxy to frontend [tr_326259fa9793] — which fits the alert set (load-generator, frontend-proxy, frontend, checkout, cart all firing at the same second) being one caller-chain propagation originating at or below frontend. The cart image flap [tr_02e67517a613] ended ~57 minutes before onset with the pre-hotfix reference live, so it is not the mechanism. I name frontend as the likely locus, but the mechanism is unidentified: no latency or saturation series was ever returned, and no specialist examined frontend or any downstream service.
verdict.reasoning: The well-supported result is negative: cart cannot be the error surface, since its error ratio is exactly zero across 128 incident samples with zero undefined intervals [tr_6696564ceed5][tr_7f64a0cb0538], and its logs show ordinary cart-store operations continuing two minutes past onset [tr_185f3cb170bc] — ruling out crash, stall and store disconnection. The change log looks dramatic (four update/revert pairs cycling a hotfix image) but the last landed ~57 minutes before onset and the pre-hotfix artifact was live at the start [tr_02e67517a613]; a flap that ended an hour earlier with the service serving cleanly is a change record, not a failing mechanism. What points away from cart is the trace result: the degrading hop is always in load-generator, frontend, or frontend-proxy-to-frontend [tr_326259fa9793], matching the alerted set exactly as a request path. Hence frontend. I attach no fault class because the traces pointing there are from 00:58-00:59 and are explicitly disclaimed as unable to characterise 01:13:31 [tr_326259fa9793], and no latency, CPU, memory or pool series was returned for anything [tr_7f64a0cb0538].
open_questions: No dispatch examined frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout, or the 14 unmeasured edges — the named service is inferred from cart-side traces, never observed.
What signal actually tripped the alert at 01:13:31? No latency or saturation series was retrieved for any service [tr_7f64a0cb0538].

Tempo shows no cart traces after 00:59:34 while span metrics report defined cart values in every incident interval [tr_326259fa9793][tr_7f64a0cb0538]; this tension is unresolved, and cart's logs at the onset second fall in a truncated gap [tr_185f3cb170bc].

alternatives.root_cause: A latency or capacity problem in frontend-proxy or a checkout-side dependency slowed the shared request path, with frontend merely relaying the wait.
alternatives.why_not: Equally unexamined; the sampled traces attribute degrading hops to frontend route execution as often as to the proxy-to-frontend edge, and no pre-onset trace can distinguish them.

alternatives.root_cause: The repeated cart image update/revert cycle left cart on an unintended or null artifact reference whose effects surfaced later.
alternatives.why_not: Cart served continuously with zero errors and normal store operations through and after onset [tr_7f64a0cb0538][tr_185f3cb170bc], and nothing landed in the 57 minutes before the start [tr_02e67517a613].

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any series is expected. The observable consequence of abstaining is that the alert set (load-generator, frontend-proxy, frontend, checkout, cart) continues in whatever state it is in, and the next investigative dispatch — latency percentiles and saturation for frontend and frontend-proxy, and traces covering 01:13:31 rather than 00:58–00:59 — has an unperturbed system to measure. Acting now would destroy that baseline.
proposal.if_wrong: Abstention is wrong if the incident is in fact still active and degrading user-visible checkout traffic, and a frontend restart would have cleared it. That would show as frontend error ratio or p95 latency remaining elevated across the next measurement window while frontend-proxy->frontend spans keep absorbing the degrading hop. Note the falsifier cannot be evaluated from the evidence in hand: no latency or saturation series was ever returned for any service [tr_7f64a0cb0538], and Tempo returned no cart traces after 00:59:34 [tr_326259fa9793], so the signal that actually tripped the alert at 01:13:31 has never been observed. That is precisely why no action is proposed.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is continued exposure if the incident is live. The risk of the alternative — restarting or rolling back frontend on this evidence — is higher and concrete: frontend is named only by inference from cart-side traces sampled ~14 minutes before onset, and no specialist ever examined it. restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state; none exists for frontend. rollback_image and revert_config require a recorded prior image or config for the target inside the window; the only change history retrieved is cart's [tr_02e67517a613], and it ends ~57 minutes before onset with the pre-hotfix reference already live, so even cart fails the precondition. A rollback of cart would re-apply a flapping hotfix image that the evidence rules out as the mechanism, and would reset a service that is demonstrably clean on all three signal types [tr_6696564ceed5][tr_185f3cb170bc].
proposal.blast_radius: None from this proposal. For contrast, the action not taken: recreating frontend would reset connections for frontend-proxy and load-generator upstream and interrupt in-flight calls to ad, product-reviews, recommendation and checkout (and through checkout to currency, email, payment, product-catalog, shipping) — the whole alerting caller chain, to chase a locus that was never directly observed.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Five services across the checkout path alerted simultaneously, which is a coordinated multi-service failure rather than a single warning latency blip. No open incident covers it, and the shared downstream dependencies (cart/checkout fan-out) give specialists a clear place to start.
